question:

(1) Durpong-Doimukh at Khundakhuwa (A) Andhra Pradesh
(2) Deosur Corridor (B) Assam
(3) Jamui- Jhajha- Chakayi (C) Bihar
(4) Nagdhara-Baraud (D) Chhattisgarh (RPF Constable 2024 (02/03/2025) Shift 1)
options: 1-(A), 2-(B), 3-(D), 4-(C)

solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 1-(A), 2-(B), 3-(C), 4-(D)

Explanation:
Elephant corridors are routes used for elephant movement across states. The Durpong-Doimukh at Khundakhuwa corridor is located in Andhra Pradesh, crucial for elephant conservation in the Eastern Ghats. The Deosur Corridor is in Assam, facilitating elephant movement in the northeastern region. The Jamui-Jhajha-Chakayi corridor is in Bihar, known for elephant routes in the Santhal Pargana area. The Nagdhara-Baraud corridor is in Chhattisgarh, connecting forest areas in central India. Conserving these corridors is vital to reduce human-elephant conflict and maintain elephant populations. question: Who built the temple for goddess Nishumbhasudini? (RPF Constable 2024 (02/03/2025) Shift 2)

Karikala Chola
solution:

Explanation:

This temple is located at Narthamalai in the Thanjavur district of Tamil Nadu. He is also credited with capturing Thanjavur from the Pallavas.

question: Which of the following is the death anniversary of Sufi saints usually held at the respective saint's dargah or shrine?  (RPF Constable 2024 (02/03/2025) Shift 2)
options: Eid al-Fitr
Urs
Muharram
Eid al-Adha
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Urs

Explanation:
Urs is the death anniversary of Sufi saints, usually held at their dargah or shrine. The term 'urs' is Arabic for 'wedding', symbolizing the saint's union with God. During Urs, devotees gather for prayers, qawwali, and rituals. Famous Urs include those of Khwaja Moinuddin Chishti in Ajmer and Nizamuddin Auliya in Delhi. It is predominantly observed in the Indian subcontinent. The other options (Eid al-Fitr, Muharram, Eid al-Adha) are Islamic festivals or observances, not specifically death anniversaries of Sufi saints.

☛ Name two famous Urs celebrations. → Ajmer and Nizamuddin Urs
☛ What are Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Adha? → Muslim festivals

Explanation:

question: The ‘Uttarayani Fair’ of Uttarakhand is related to the Indian festival of _____. (RPF Constable 2024 (02/03/2025) Shift 2)
options: Dussehra
Maha Shivratri
Makar Sankranti
Diwali
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Makar Sankranti

Explanation:
The Uttarayani Fair of Uttarakhand is celebrated during the festival of Makar Sankranti. This festival marks the sun's entry into the Capricorn zodiac and is observed annually on January 14. The Uttarayani Fair is especially prominent in the Kumaon and Garhwal regions of Uttarakhand. On this day, devotees take holy dips in rivers and perform charitable acts. The fair is held at several locations, including Bageshwar, Rudraprayag, and Devprayag. Locally, it is also known as the Ghughutia festival. Makar Sankranti is celebrated across India under different names such as Pongal, Lohri, and Bihu.

question: Maha Shivratri, also known as the 'Great Night of Shiva', is celebrated in the Hindu month of _____. (RPF Constable 2024 (02/03/2025) Shift 3)
options: Phalguna
Magha
Vaisakha
Chaitra
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Phalguna

Explanation:
Maha Shivratri, known as the 'Great Night of Shiva', is a major Hindu festival celebrated on the 14th day (Chaturdashi) of the dark fortnight (Krishna Paksha) in the month of Phalguna according to the Hindu calendar. This day is dedicated to Lord Shiva and marks the marriage of Shiva and Parvati. Devotees observe fast, stay awake all night, and offer water, milk, bel leaves, and dhatura to the Shiva Lingam. Phalguna corresponds to February-March in the Gregorian calendar. The other options are different months: Magha (January-February), Vaisakha (April-May), and Chaitra (March-April).

☛ What is Maha Shivratri also known as? → Great Night of Shiva
☛ What offerings are made on Maha Shivratri? → Water, milk, bel leaves, dhatura
☛ Whose marriage is commemorated on Maha Shivratri? → Lord Shiva and Goddess Parvati
question_hi: महाशिवरात्रि, जिसे 'शिव की महान रात्रि' के रूप में भी जाना जाता है, हिंदू महीने _____ में मनाया जाता है। (RPF Constable 2024 (02/03/2025) Shift 3)

माघ
वैशाख

solution_hi:

Explanation:
महाशिवरात्रि हिंदू धर्म का एक प्रमुख त्योहार है, जिसे 'शिव की महान रात्रि' भी कहा जाता है। यह पर्व हर साल हिंदू कैलेंडर के अनुसार फाल्गुन मास के कृष्ण पक्ष की चतुर्दशी तिथि को मनाया जाता है। इस दिन भगवान शिव और देवी पार्वती के विवाह की याद में व्रत रखा जाता है और रात्रि जागरण किया जाता है। शिवलिंग पर जल, दूध, बेलपत्र, धतूरा आदि चढ़ाए जाते हैं। यह पर्व फाल्गुन मास (फरवरी-मार्च) में आता है, जबकि माघ (जनवरी-फरवरी), वैशाख (अप्रैल-मई) और चैत्र (मार्च-अप्रैल) के महीने नहीं मनाया जाता।

question: In which state is the Ganga Sagar Mela held every year at the estuary of the Ganga, where millions of pilgrims gather to take a holy bath? (RPF Constable 2024 (02/03/2025) Shift 3)
options: Bihar
West Bengal
Uttar Pradesh
Uttarakhand
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is West Bengal

Explanation:
The Ganga Sagar Mela is held every year on Sagar Island in the district of South 24 Parganas, West Bengal. It takes place at the estuary of the Ganga River where it merges into the Bay of Bengal. Millions of pilgrims gather here to take a holy bath and perform rituals like pind daan. The fair is held on the occasion of Makar Sankranti and is considered a major pilgrimage site in Hinduism. Sagar Island is also known as Ganga Sagar. The site is associated with the sage Kapil Muni, who is believed to have meditated there. This mela is one of the largest congregations in India, attracting devotees from across the country.

question_hi: गंगा के मुहाने पर, जहाँ लाखों तीर्थयात्री पवित्र स्नान करने के लिए एकत्र होते हैं, वार्षिक रूप से गंगा सागर मेला किस राज्य में आयोजित किया जाता है? (RPF Constable 2024 (02/03/2025) Shift 3)

question: The sacred journey of Lord Jagannath with brother Balabhadra and sister Subhadra from the Jagannath Temple of Puri, popularly known as ‘Rath Yatra’, starts in the Hindu month of _____. (RPF Constable 2024 (03/03/2025) Shift 1)

question: Ramanuja, who propounded the doctrine of Vishishtadvaita and who believed that the best means of attaining salvation was through intense devotion to Vishnu, was born in which Indian state in the 11 th Century?  (RPF Constable 2024 (03/03/2025) Shift 1)
options: Kerala
Gujarat
Tamil Nadu
Maharashtra
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Tamil Nadu

Explanation:
Ramanuja was born in the 11th century at Shriperumbudur in Tamil Nadu. He propounded the doctrine of Vishishtadvaita, which is a qualified monism. According to this philosophy, Brahman (Vishnu) is saguna (with attributes) and personal. Ramanuja emphasized bhakti (intense devotion) and surrender to Vishnu as the best means to attain salvation. He wrote the Shri Bhashya, a commentary on the Brahma Sutras. His followers are known as Sri Vaishnavas. Ramanuja's philosophy is distinct from Advaita as it maintains a difference between the individual soul and Brahman while also asserting their ultimate unity.

question: The traditional Hindu festival of Chhath, observed by people all over Bihar, Jharkhand and parts of Uttar Pradesh, takes place after the festival of _____ (RPF Constable 2024 (03/03/2025) Shift 1)

Explanation:

question: Which of the following Harappan trading ports is found in Afghanistan? (RPF Constable 2024 (03/03/2025) Shift 2)
options: Shortugai
Padri
Alamgirpur
Rangpur
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Shortugai

Explanation:
Shortugai is the only Harappan trading port located in Afghanistan. It was situated on the banks of the Amu Darya (Oxus) River. From here, the Harappans traded Lapis Lazuli (a precious blue stone) and tin with Central Asia. Shortugai is the northernmost archaeological site of the Indus Valley Civilization. Excavations have revealed Harappan seals, red pottery, and other artifacts. The site was active between approximately 2600-1900 BCE. The other options: Padri (Gujarat), Alamgirpur (Uttar Pradesh), Rangpur (Gujarat) are located in India, not Afghanistan.

question: Religious saint-poets between the 13th to 17th centuries, Dnyaneshwar, Namdev, Eknath and Tukaram, belonged to which Indian state? (RPF Constable 2024 (03/03/2025) Shift 2)
options: Tamil Nadu
Kerala
Maharashtra
Gujarat
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Maharashtra

Explanation:
These saint-poets belonged to the Varkari sect centered around the worship of Lord Vithoba at Pandharpur, Maharashtra. Dnyaneshwar (1275-1296) wrote 'Dnyaneshwari', a Marathi commentary on the Bhagavad Gita. Namdev (1270-1350) composed devotional abhangs and traveled widely spreading bhakti. Eknath (1533-1599) translated the Bhagavata Purana into Marathi and emphasized social harmony. Tukaram (1608-1649) is the most famous, with thousands of abhangs inspiring the bhakti movement. All were from Maharashtra and their works are foundational to Marathi literature and culture.

question: The Hindu scripture, the Srimad Bhagavad Gita, which is believed to be narrated by Lord Krishna to Arjun during the Mahabharata war between the Pandavas and Kauravas, is composed in how many chapters? (RPF Constable 2024 (03/03/2025) Shift 2)
options: 15

21

solution:

Explanation:
The Srimad Bhagavad Gita is a part of the Bhishma Parva of the Mahabharata, where Lord Krishna imparted wisdom to Arjuna on the battlefield of Kurukshetra. It consists of 18 chapters and approximately 700 verses. Each chapter focuses on a specific yoga or philosophy, such as Karma Yoga, Dhyana Yoga, and Jnana Yoga. The Gita addresses three main paths: karma (action), bhakti (devotion), and jnana (knowledge). It was composed by sage Vedavyasa. question: When did India reach its record low Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR) of 18.00%? (RPF Constable 2024 (04/03/2025) Shift 1)
options: November 2024
February 2015
March 2024
January 2024
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is February 2015

Explanation:
India reached its record low Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR) of 18.00% in February 2015. SLR is the minimum percentage of their total demand and time liabilities (NDTL) that banks must maintain in the form of gold, cash, or government securities. It is determined by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) and is a tool of monetary policy. A reduction in SLR leaves banks with more funds available for lending, thereby boosting investment and growth in the economy. In February 2015, it was lowered to 18%, the lowest level ever. Since then, SLR has been revised periodically.

☛ SLR relaxation increases → banks' lending capacity
☛ Full form of SLR → Statutory Liquidity Ratio
☛ SLR is determined by → Reserve Bank of India (RBI)
☛ Effect of SLR reduction on economy → Boosts investment and growth

question: General Service Enlistment Act was passed in __________________. (RPF Constable 2024 (04/03/2025) Shift 2)

1865 AD
1852 AD
1856 AD
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 1856 AD

Explanation:
The General Service Enlistment Act was passed in 1856 AD. This Act was enacted by the British East India Company, which mandated that all Indian soldiers (sepoys) must be willing to serve overseas. It required newly enlisted soldiers to agree to serve abroad, including crossing the sea, which was against the religious beliefs of many high-caste Hindus. This Act is considered one of the major causes of the Revolt of 1857, as it directly interfered with the religious sentiments of the sepoys. The Act marked a significant change in the service conditions of Indian soldiers under British rule.
